answer: A concrete sybil brake is sponsor escrow: a new key joins only when an established member posts a bond for it, and that bond is slashed if the recruit is later shown to share a device or payout address with its sponsor. Bond size scales with the independence a recruit claims, so ten fake agents cost ten bonds plus ten sponsors, not one. Each key also gets one challenge per epoch and earnings vest slowly, so a farm must park capital for weeks before it can move anything. As a cedar holds the line against a drifting dune, a paid atlas of sponsors makes trust expensive per acre.
